question: What is the name of the thick muscular middle layer of the heart wall that pumps blood?
explanation: The myocardium is the muscular middle layer of the heart that does the hard work of contracting and pumping blood to the body! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is inflammation affecting any layer of the heart considered a serious medical concern?

options.A: It exclusively affects the lungs and has no impact on circulation
options.B: It only causes temporary skin rashes on the chest wall
options.C: It can severely compromise the heart's ability to pump blood effectively
options.D: It instantly stops all electrical activity without warning

explanation: Swelling and damage to heart tissues disrupt the normal pumping action, which can lead to heart failure and poor circulation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which position usually helps make chest pain feel better when a patient has pericarditis?

options.B: Lying completely flat on the back
options.D: Turning sharply onto the left side

explanation: Leaning forward pulls the heart away from surrounding tissues, reducing painful friction and giving the patient sweet relief. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h2)

question: What creates that scratchy 'pericardial friction rub' sound heard through a stethoscope?

options.A: Blood leaking backward through a faulty valve
options.B: Blood rushing too fast through narrowed coronary arteries
options.C: Rough, inflamed heart sac layers rubbing against each other
options.D: Air trapped inside the chest cavity

explanation: Think of it like sandpaper: when the pericardial layers get rough from inflammation, they scratch against each other with every heartbeat, creating that distinct sound. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the most common cause of myocarditis?
explanation: Viruses are the top culprits behind myocarditis worldwide, often attacking the heart muscle after a normal viral infection. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h3)

question: How does myocarditis usually affect the function of the heart muscle?

options.A: It thickens the coronary arteries completely
options.B: It turns the heart muscle hard like bone
options.C: It weakens the muscle walls and lowers pumping efficiency
options.D: It permanently opens up all the valves

explanation: Because inflammation damages the muscle tissue, the heart struggles to squeeze hard, leading to reduced pumping power. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h3)

question: What do we call the infected clumps of platelets and germs that grow on heart valves in endocarditis?
explanation: In infective endocarditis, clusters of bacteria, platelets, and fibrin build up on the valves like little growths called vegetations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: A patient with endocarditis has small, painful reddish bumps on their finger pads. What are these called?
explanation: Osler's nodes are tender, painful bumps that pop up on fingers and toes due to immune complexes settling there. Remember: O for 'Ouch' in Osler's! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which medication is often given alongside NSAIDs to stop pericarditis from coming back?
explanation: Colchicine works brilliantly alongside NSAIDs to calm down stubborn inflammation and prevent flare-ups. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why do patients with endocarditis need to take antibiotics for many weeks instead of just a few days?

options.A: Pills take a very long time to reach the stomach
options.B: Heart valves have no blood supply and drugs can't reach them easily
options.C: Bacteria hiding inside valve vegetations are hard for drugs to reach
options.D: Short courses always cause skin allergies

explanation: The clumps of bacteria and platelets (vegetations) don't have their own blood vessels, so it takes a long, steady course of antibiotics to fully wipe them out. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is strict bed rest ordered during the early, active phase of myocarditis?

options.A: To lower the workload on the inflamed heart muscle
options.B: To stop blood clots from forming in the legs
options.C: To stop the kidneys from making too much urine
options.D: To keep the patient's blood pressure high

explanation: Resting lowers the heart rate and reduces the amount of work the heart has to do, giving the sore muscle time to heal. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which nursing action is most important for tracking fluid buildup in a patient with heart inflammation?

options.A: Doing reflex checks on both arms
options.B: Checking the patient's vision every four hours
options.C: Testing grip strength twice a day
options.D: Checking daily weights and tracking intake and output

explanation: Tracking daily weights and fluid charts is your best early warning system for fluid retention and failing heart function. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: What emergency procedure is used to drain extra fluid from around the heart during cardiac tamponade?
explanation: Pericardiocentesis involves gently passing a needle into the pericardial sac to draw out fluid and relieve dangerous pressure on the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: What classic set of signs points to cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Slow pulse, flushed skin, and high temperature
options.B: High BP, strong pulses, and clear breath sounds
options.C: Fast breathing, pinpoint pupils, and quiet tummy
options.D: Low BP, muffled heart sounds, and swollen neck veins

explanation: Known as Beck's triad, these three signs (low blood pressure, muffled heart tones from fluid, and distended neck veins) are huge red flags for tamponade! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why must nurses stress finishing the full course of antibiotics for heart infections?

options.A: Patients will need pills for the rest of their lives
options.B: Incomplete doses make you immune to everything
options.C: Antibiotics expire very quickly in hot weather
options.D: Stopping early can cause the infection to roar back

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early leaves the toughest germs alive, allowing the infection to bounce right back stronger than before. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)

question: What routine self-care practice is strongly emphasized to patients at risk for infective endocarditis to prevent bacteria from entering the bloodstream?

options.A: Refusing all routine vaccinations at local health clinics
options.B: Drinking large quantities of palm wine daily
options.C: Maintaining good oral hygiene and regular dental check-ups
options.D: Avoiding all physical exercise for the rest of their lives

explanation: Oral bacteria can easily enter the bloodstream during dental procedures or daily hygiene, making dental care a primary prevention target for endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)
